title: Build multi-candidate generate/critique/repair loop with deterministic Python selection
success_test: Implement or use a loop that generates 16-32 diverse candidate IR programs/rules, runs critique and critique-the-critique/repair passes, parses candidates fail-closed, scores all candidates with deterministic Python on permitted public training pairs, and ranks candidates by exact metrics rather than model confidence. Success requires at least 8 parseable non-duplicate candidates and either >=1 exact train-consistent candidate on the selected task or a dominant mechanically observed failure class that predeclares one next ablation. Protocol: lab/experiments/T0022-multi-candidate-critique-verify-loop.json.
required_resources: validated rule/lattice IR executor and exact scorer
permitted public ARC training data only
authorized NVIDIA NIM execution path for target-model proposal generation
expected_artifacts: sanitized model response cache or hashes
evidence: User/operator requested moving beyond a single model answer toward multiple reasoning/generation paths, model critique and critique-of-critique, with Python selecting the best candidate. This is supported by ARC-R030 and ARC-R032: parseability improved but exact candidate coverage stayed 0/2, implying that one-shot proposal quality remains a bottleneck. ARC-R035 further showed a large reachable search graph without exact fit, motivating broader proposal distributions plus deterministic verification.
initial_task_selection_policy: Prefer 06df4c85 after T0021 resolves because ARC-R032 executed lattice programs there but remained exact-wrong. Use 0607ce86 only after T0021 produces durable failure taxonomy or explicitly freezes a compatible mechanism.
guardrails: Python exact execution/scoring is the judge
do not invent model outputs, scores, CI success, or provider behavior
evolve one variable at a time if rejected
